body: Can you provide a small example application that allows to reproduce your issue?
I encountered this error message as well after the upgrade to 3.4.11, and then some minutes later it dissappeared. No clue what triggered it or what made it go away again.
Try manually clearing your cache - e.g. `rm -rf var/cache/*` to see if it fixes things - it could just be that the upgrade left the old cache in a weird state.

I just found the solution to this. I was missing the `security` configuration. After adding a simple 

```
security:
    providers:
        in_memory:
            memory: ~
    firewalls:
        main:
            anonymous: ~
```

to my `config.yml` everything worked just fine. I'm wondering if there is any way to completely disable the security part since, as you can see, I'm not really using it.

If you're not using security at all, I think you can just disable/remove the `SecurityBundle` from your kernel. That would disable the feature causing the problem. 

But, I also think there is a *small* bug in the core. It is this setup:

A) `SecurityBundle` is installed
B) But, security is not enabled - because the security config is empty (see the top of `SecurityExtension`).

This causes `security.http_utils` to not load (and other services). But, the `AddSessionDomainConstraintPass` IS still activated, which fails due to the missing service.

Thank's for the hint - after removing `SecurityBundle` from my kernel as well as from my configuration everything works fine.

I also think this is a small bug since `AddSessionDomainConstraintPass` should only check for `security.http_utils` if security is enabled.

@weaverryan not checking whether the service was defined or no in the compiler pass is something that @nicolas-grekas decided to do on purpose when working on the security fix (but it is not necessary for the fix itself in the current state).
Now we have a reproducer so that we can work on a fix + realistic test case :)
